title: context-report
summary: Produce, verify, attest: how chock's eval export and context-report's producers write a report, how verify checks it, and what the spec says about signing it.
intro: A context-report is an in-toto Statement/v1 about one artifact for one agent, with one row per measured fact. Each row says whether anyone can recompute it (re-derivable) or only the author reports it (claimed), and the report never gives one pass or fail for the whole artifact. chock can export its policies' eval cases in context-report's run/v0.1 format. context-report produces the rows and writes the statement; verify checks it is well-formed and bound to the artifact by digest. Signing is described in the spec; at this pin no code in context-report signs a report.

boundaries.label: Attest: what the spec asks, and what the repo signs

nodes.label: chock eval export
nodes.card: chock eval export --format context-report --out DIR takes each policy's tier-3 cases (those with no execute block in evals/suite.yaml). It writes the rule lines chock renders into subjects/<id>.md, one evals/<case>/prompt.md and graders/expect.md per case, and a run.json with no models and no judge filled in. chock does not import context-report.

nodes.label: run/v0.1 manifest
nodes.card: The input to context-report run: the subjects, the target agent, the subject models, the tasks and how many runs per arm. Tasks can be a directory of cases (prompt.md plus graders/*.md), which run/evalcases.py compiles. It is metadata only; what an artifact does is read from the artifact.

nodes.label: context-report run
nodes.card: Checks the manifest before any model call, then, for each subject and model, records the arms' transcripts under out/runs/<run id>/ and writes one statement through produce_statement. This is the path that calls the subject and judge models named in the manifest.

nodes.label: efficacy row
nodes.card: Builds the efficacy row from graded arms: the task run with the rule prepended and without it (the prompt-prefix-v1 ablation). It reports the lift with a 95% Newcombe interval, and its basis is always claimed.

nodes.label: Recorded payloads
nodes.card: Per-target pre-tool-use payload shapes, and where a deny appears in a hook's stdout. The file says they were taken from agentseam's vendor data.

nodes.label: produce_statement
nodes.card: context-report produce digests the subject, then runs the artifact's own hook command on recorded payloads for the reachability, fault and cost rows. Every v0.1 attribute gets a row; one it cannot measure says NotAvailable or NotApplicable and why. Nothing under produce/ imports a network or model module.

nodes.label: Row rules
nodes.card: A row is refused when it breaks a rule: a re-derivable row must carry an inputHash (sha256 over the subject digest, target, client version, attribute and inputs), an unmeasured row must give its reasoning, and efficacy must be claimed.

nodes.label: in-toto Statement
nodes.card: Wraps the rows in one in-toto Statement/v1 per subject digest and target, with the context-report v0.1 predicateType. The digest is sha256 of a file, or of a sorted list of each file's path and sha256 for a directory. validate() checks it against the v0.1 schema shipped in the package.

nodes.label: report.json
nodes.card: The statement as JSON: subject[0].digest.sha256 names the artifact, and predicate.attributes holds the rows, each with its basis and result. The cited file is the spec's worked example.

nodes.label: verify_statement
nodes.card: context-report verify REPORT --subject PATH validates the schema, recomputes the subject digest and lists each row as re-derivable, claimed or unmeasured. It ends with well-formed and bound: True or False, and exits 1 on a schema error or a digest mismatch. It does not re-run any row and never grades the artifact.

nodes.label: recompute_rows
nodes.card: A function in verify.py, not a CLI command: for each re-derivable row it asks a Recomputer for the row again and compares result, values and measurement. Claimed rows are skipped. The only built-in Recomputer checks that the row has an inputHash; it does not re-run the measurement.

nodes.label: to_svr verdict
nodes.card: A function in verify.py, not a CLI command: it turns a verification into an in-toto statement with an SVR v0.2 predicate, whose subject is the report's own digest and whose properties say well-formed, bound and how many rows are claimed. It does not sign anything.

nodes.label: release.yml
nodes.card: On a published GitHub Release, builds the wheel and sdist, publishes them to PyPI, signs them with Sigstore and attaches the signature bundles. This signs the context-report package, not a report.

nodes.label: Signing (spec)
nodes.card: The spec says a producer SHOULD emit the statement through actions/attest (a DSSE envelope in a Sigstore bundle, signed with the CI workflow's identity and logged in Rekor), and a consumer checks it with gh attestation verify --predicate-type. At this pin no workflow runs actions/attest, and spec/index.md names an attest.yml workflow the repo does not contain.
